description:
With Don Fraser; an epically successful search for several rarities (Vermilion Flycatcher, Tropical Kingbird, Dickcissel, and especially Tricolored Munias); several other birders (including Ron & Lori Smith and Holly & Mark Salvato) were present at our arrival or arrived later. We parked in the parking lot and walked to the observation tower, then back toward the parking lot, then back to the tower, then west to about halfway around the lake, then back and forth several times between the tower and the parking lot, then after finding the munias, we drove to two wetlands (the marina and the boat ramp) between the parking lot and the one-lane bridge. The weather was overcast, 54 degrees ("feels like" 51), and breezy at the start, warming up somewhat by the end but remaining overcast and breezy; we never saw the sun. We saw at least 4 Painted Buntings but did not find the apparent Painted Bunting x Indigo Bunting that Bob Wallace discovered earlier this week; we both really wanted to see this bird and were always looking for it. We saw 17 (!) Brown Pelicans, of which 3 were metal-banded. Is somebody releasing rehabbed pelicans here after banding them? We left at 1204 and headed into town for a Subway lunch. After a stop at Val's home to drop off some supplies, Don and I headed back north. I arrived home at 1756.

P.S. I am pleased to state that we did not see any birder iPodding any of the rarities.

"One More Colour Abnormal Bird in Jabalpur"

Leucistic Tricolored Munia  or  Lonchura malacca with a pigment abnormality Colour Coding resulting in reduced or absent melanin, causing pale or white patches on the plumage due to Water Pollution or Malnutrition. It's a Fifth bird species of city which is suffering with this deformity, needs more observation and research in this problem.
Maybe it is an indication of some upcoming big problem in birds.
We (Dr Aamir Nasirabadi and me) had observed this bird in the airport road today, in the same place where we had found that leucistic Large Grey Warble near water Lake.
